sources.fullCitation: Eberhard Görner, Walter Jurmann: Sein Leben, seine Musik. Leipzig: Henschel, 2014. 280 pp., with a CD. Werkverzeichnis, pp. 200–217, arranged by year; its note 10 states that the work list, filmography and discography rest on the information at www.jurmann.org.
sources.title: Görner, Walter Jurmann: Sein Leben, seine Musik — Werkverzeichnis
sources.creator: Eberhard Görner
sources.researchNote: A secondary work list, arranged by year. By its own note it follows the Walter Jurmann website, so it does not corroborate the online works catalogue (SRC0306) independently. It is a different work from Alexander Sieghardt’s catalogue in Buxbaum (SRC0373); until November 2026 the archive’s notes took it for Sieghardt’s “year-by-year list”.

works.title: Wings of the Morning
works.publicNote: IMDb lists “Marche militaire” from Les nuits moscovites (1934), with music by Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann, as heard uncredited in the film; no other source says so, and the credits of the time name Muir Mathieson as music director (the copyright registrations) and Arthur Benjamin for the music (Hollywood Spectator). The Walter Jurmann works catalogue and Görner’s work list, which follows it, record background music Jurmann and Kaper wrote for the film as not used; Sieghardt’s filmography names Arthur Benjamin and, with a question mark, Jurmann for the music.

works.title: Little Boy Blue
works.publicNote: MGM one-reel Miniature after Eugene Field’s poem, directed by Harold S. Bucquet, registered by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer on 22 May 1936 and released on 23 May. Sieghardt’s filmography describes this film, produced by Jack Chertok and with Chic Sale, and credits its background music to Jurmann with Kaper, who were then under contract at MGM; no document of the time names a composer. His release date, 30 July 1936, and the “animated short” of Görner’s work list and the Jurmann catalogue belong to another Little Boy Blue of 1936, Ub Iwerks’s ComiColor cartoon released by Celebrity Productions that day. The archive recorded that cartoon here until November 2026.

works.title: Es war einmal ein Baby
works.publicNote: Children’s song from Melodie der Liebe, listed as “Kinderlied (Es war einmal ein Baby)” on the film’s song folio and under “Kinderlied” in the Walter Jurmann works catalogue.

works.title: Vivons l’amour, vivons la vie
works.publicNote: Sieghardt’s opus list also names Paul Bertrand among the authors of the words.

titleVariants.note: Sieghardt’s title for the song (opus list, p. 185), with “Es war einmal ein Baby” as the first line of the refrain. Görner’s work list has the same title (1931, p. 203).

timelineEvents.title: End of the Jurmann–Kaper partnership
timelineEvents.label: 1938 · Jurmann–Kaper era ends
timelineEvents.shortDescription: The last music registered in the names of both Kaper and Jurmann dates from February 1939.
timelineEvents.longDescription: The last work registered in the names of both composers is “At night”, a cue for The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn written with Franz Waxman and registered in the United States on 25 February 1939. Sieghardt’s catalogue and Görner’s work list name two later songs by the pair, “Harbour Café”, published by Criterion in 1941, and “Blush and Sigh”, written for When Ladies Meet (1941) and not used; no document of the time confirms either. No document in the archive gives the reasons the partnership ended.

contributions.publicNote: The BnF catalogue of the voice-only edition names Léo Lelièvre (1899–1966) among the lyricists. Its separate voice-and-piano entry names Varna and Marc-Cab without Lelièvre; the copies have not been compared.
contributions.scopeNote: The Columbia disc catalogue transcribes “Varna, Lelievre & Marc-Cab” without a forename. The BnF catalogue for the voice-only edition identifies Léo Lelièvre (1899–1966); the voice-and-piano entry does not list him. The attribution remains probable pending comparison of the printed sources.
